messages:
Aisha: taking primary for the nightcap shift. I’m online until 07:00 PT. Quick notes up front: only Carlos is listed as backup for the model-serving pager tonight, Ben is secondary but traveling. If you get paged and can’t reach me, page Carlos immediately and escalate to Ben after 10m. :rotating_light:

Aisha: coverage gaps: reduced on-call headcount on infra team (only one infra engineer until 02:00). if anything touching autoscaler/cluster hits, treat as priority and shout in #eng-sre.

IncidentBot: [ALERT] model-serving-high-latency triggered (policy: p95 latency > 400ms, 3m window). Incident ID: INC-2024-8347.

Carlos: I saw the alert. quick remediation cheatsheet below — follow in order and stop once latency drops.
Carlos: 1) Check autoscaler and node pressure
  - kubectl get hpa -n model-serving
  - kubectl top nodes | sort -k2 -n
Carlos: 2) Check model-worker pods for OOM or crashloop:
```sh
kubectl -n model-serving get pods -o wide | grep model-worker
kubectl -n model-serving logs <pod> -c model-runtime --tail=200
```
Carlos: 3) If KV cache misses are high, consider clearing prefix cache for the affected model (low risk, short ttl). Run the cache flush playbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/cache-flush (use playbook-runner).

Ben: if you hit sustained p95 > 600ms or customers start complaining, do these next steps: fallback to compatible lower-latency model variant (quantized-v2) and enable prefix caching knob. Fallback command (console/API):
```json
POST /v1/deployments/<route>/rollback
{ "model": "open-quantized-v2", "traffic": 0.3 }
```
Ben: Also update the incident timeline and ping CS with the customer-impact template: https://redwood.internal/incidents/status-template (fill severity, affected routes, ETA).

Dana: if GPU memory OOMs are present in logs, try restart of the offending pod and set MAX_BATCH_SIZE=1 temporarily, or deploy a cpu-fallback replica group. Commands:
```sh
kubectl -n model-serving delete pod <pod> --grace-period=30
# temp k8s patch to set env
kubectl -n model-serving set env deploy/model-worker MAX_BATCH_SIZE=1
```
Dana: note: if you restart, mark the restart in timeline with reason.

Aisha: handoff checklist I’m leaving in case you take over mid-shift:
- current incidents: INC-2024-8347 (model latency, mitigating with autoscaler + possible fallback)
- last deploy: model-serving v2.14 rolled at 23:40 PT (rollback safe window ends +2h)
- primary contacts: Aisha (me) -> Carlos -> Ben (escalation) -> Dana (SRE consult)
- runbooks: model latency: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/model-latency-playbook, cluster autoscaler: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/autoscaler-troubleshoot

Carlos: quick quick pointers for page handlers (this is the minimal checklist to copy into your timeline):
- confirm alert scope (routes, regions)
- check infra/worker pod health and GPU metrics
- restart single pod, observe 5m, escalate if not improved
- fallback to quantized model if latency not improving after 10m
- notify CS if > 15m customer impact

Ben: paging/escalation rules reminder: first page -> 2m ack window -> auto-remind at 6m -> escalate to secondary at 10m. Use /page @oncall if urgent.

IncidentBot: NOTE: please add timeline entries using /incident add <id> "<note>" so we keep the audit.

Aisha: final notes: if you need to rotate primary for any reason, post here and add the new primary and ETA for the swap. keep messages short and explicit. I’ll leave notifications on and will watch for escalations for the next 30m before powering down for a meeting. :thumbsup:
